## Professional Identity

Ben Bubnick is a Principal-level Data Engineer and Data Scientist with over a decade of experience building reliable data infrastructure at the intersection of healthcare and enterprise data systems. He is known for untangling complex, multi-source data environments — turning messy, inconsistent inputs into trustworthy, production-grade pipelines — and for producing documentation and knowledge transfer artifacts that outlast him at every organization. His deepest domain expertise is healthcare data integration: FHIR, HL7, EHR systems, and clinical interoperability at scale.

## What Meaningful Work Looks Like

Ben is motivated primarily by personal satisfaction from solving real, concrete problems — the kind where there's a clear upstream mess and a clear downstream improvement. Compensation and stability are his top current priorities, followed by healthcare outcomes impact. He does not need a cause to feel engaged, but healthcare is the domain where his skills are deepest and his interest is genuine. Work that lacks a defined problem, clear ownership, or meaningful output will not hold his attention. The role needs to have a real engineering challenge, not just a maintenance mandate.

His proudest accomplishment — managing a 70+ interconnected data source enterprise integration across multiple organizations — captures what he's built for: large-scale, high-complexity data environments where someone has to create order out of chaos and make the whole system trustworthy.

---

## Culture and Environment

Ben is most productive in collaborative, structured environments with good process and teammates who communicate well. He strongly prefers stability and clear expectations over ambiguity — he does not self-identify as someone who thrives on chaos or greenfield uncertainty, though he has delivered in those environments. His best managers have given him autonomy and trusted him to execute without micromanagement. He has no strong preference on organization size; what matters is whether the team is well-run and whether the organization genuinely supports its people. He will not stay long at a company with unclear direction or leadership that does not invest in team success.

## Career Direction

In three to five years, Ben wants to be a Staff or Principal Data Engineer recognized as the go-to expert for hard data problems — not a manager, but a technical authority whose judgment shapes how systems are built. His next role should deepen his expertise in healthcare data standards (FHIR R4/R5, USCDI, payer interoperability rules), and he is genuinely curious about applied research — the intersection of rigorous data engineering with scientific-quality analysis, which connects to his astrophysics and publication background.
